section: Nuclear power plants in India, NPCIL, civil nuclear agreements, nuclear liability law and safety (AERB)
subsections: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: Which reactor type was used in Tarapur Atomic Power Station Units 1 and 2?
accepted.x: Tarapur Units 1 and 2 are boiling water reactors (BWRs).
accepted.tq: Directly distinguish reactor types associated with different plants.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: The first unit of the Rajasthan Atomic Power Station at Rawatbhata began operation in 1972 with assistance from:
o: the United States Department of Energy
accepted.x: RAPS-1 at Rawatbhata started in 1972 with assistance from the Canadian Atomic Energy of Canada Limited (AECL).
accepted.tq: Match the project with its foreign technical collaborator.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the Kalpakkam nuclear power station?
o: It is a proposed AP1000 station in Andhra Pradesh.
It has India’s first fully indigenous PHWRs and is also associated with a PFBR.
It uses only VVER reactors supplied by Russia.
It is India’s first BWR station, located in Maharashtra.
accepted.x: Kalpakkam’s MAPS units are PHWRs representing the first fully indigenous PHWR design, and the site is also associated with a Prototype Fast Breeder Reactor (PFBR).
accepted.tq: Use a combined description to separate a plant from similar nuclear stations.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding Indian nuclear power plants:
1. Narora is located in Uttar Pradesh.
2. Narora has two 220 MW PHWR units.
3. Narora is associated with the NAPS designation.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Narora Atomic Power Station (NAPS) is in Uttar Pradesh and has two 220 MW PHWR units.
accepted.tq: Check the location, abbreviation and capacity as a single plant profile.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: Kakrapar Atomic Power Project-3 is notable as India’s first indigenous:
accepted.x: KAPP-3 is India’s first indigenous 700 MW PHWR.
accepted.tq: Identify the exact capacity attached to the ‘first indigenous’ description.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: KAPP-3 entered commercial operation on:
accepted.x: KAPP-3 commenced commercial operation on 30 June 2023.
accepted.tq: Test the precise date using closely spaced year options.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
accepted.x: Kaiga Nuclear Generating Station is located in Karnataka.
accepted.tq: Start from the sure location pair and eliminate swapped states.

accepted.s: Kaiga nuclear power station is particularly associated with:
o: the world-leading capacity factor of its units
accepted.x: Kaiga has achieved a world-leading capacity factor, exceeding 90 percent according to the plant profile.
accepted.tq: Identify the distinctive performance feature rather than the reactor type alone.

accepted.s: Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant uses which reactor technology and foreign collaboration?
accepted.x: Kudankulam uses Russian VVER pressurised water reactors (PWRs).
accepted.tq: Discriminate between reactor technology and collaborating country.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: Which of the following statements about Kudankulam Nuclear Power Plant is correct?
o: It is located in Haryana and uses PHWR technology.
Its two operating units together have a capacity of 440 MW.
Its two operating units together have a capacity of 2,000 MW and constitute the largest operating station listed here.
It is a proposed AP1000 station in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.x: Kudankulam’s two operating 1,000 MW VVER units provide 2,000 MW, making it the largest operating station in the profile.
accepted.tq: Combine unit capacity with the station-level comparison.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: Kovvada nuclear power project, as proposed, is associated with which combination?
o: Andhra Pradesh and AP1000 PWR technology from the USA
Tamil Nadu and VVER technology from Russia
accepted.x: Kovvada in Srikakulam, Andhra Pradesh, is proposed to use AP1000 pressurised water reactors supplied by the United States.
accepted.tq: Match the proposed site, state and reactor design without reversing them.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
accepted.x: Narora uses PHWRs, not VVER reactors. Gorakhpur is in Haryana, Kudankulam is in Tamil Nadu, and Kovvada is proposed in Andhra Pradesh.
accepted.tq: Find the swapped reactor type in an otherwise familiar plant-state pair.

accepted.s: The Gorakhpur Haryana Anu Vidyut Pariyojana is correctly described as:
o: two AP1000 units proposed in Andhra Pradesh
four 220 MW PHWR units operating in Uttar Pradesh
two 1,000 MW VVER units operating in Tamil Nadu
two 700 MW PHWR units under construction in Haryana
accepted.x: GHAVP consists of 700 MW PHWR units under construction in Haryana.
accepted.tq: Use the full project identity, location and capacity together.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements about the evolution of India’s PHWR design:
1. The 220 MW PHWR design was indigenised into 540 MW and 700 MW versions.
2. The 700 MW PHWR design is described as having one of the lowest costs globally.
3. The approximate cost of a 700 MW PHWR is $2 million per MW.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: India developed 540 MW and 700 MW PHWRs from the 220 MW design. The 700 MW version costs about $2 million per MW and is among the lowest-cost designs globally.
accepted.tq: Combine design lineage with the quantitative cost fact.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: Which sequence correctly represents the fleet-mode sanction of ten 700 MW PHWRs?
o: Kaiga 5–6, Gorakhpur 3–4, Chutka 1–2 and Mahi Banswara 1–4
Gorakhpur 1–2, Chutka 3–4, Mahi Banswara 5–6 and Kaiga 7–8
accepted.x: The 2017 fleet-mode sanction covered Kaiga 5–6, Gorakhpur 3–4, Chutka 1–2 and Mahi Banswara 1–4, totalling ten units.
accepted.tq: Reconstruct the sanctioned fleet from the project-unit pattern.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.x: Kudankulam Units 3–6 were listed among the nuclear projects under construction.

accepted.s: NPCIL is best described as:
o: a private company under the Ministry of Power
an autonomous IAEA body established in Vienna in 1957
a statutory safety regulator under the Ministry of Environment
a public sector enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy, registered in September 1987
accepted.x: The Nuclear Power Corporation of India Limited (NPCIL) is a public sector enterprise under the Department of Atomic Energy and was registered in September 1987.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the operating corporation from the regulator and international agency.
accepted.sec: Nuclear power plants - state and reactor type; FIRSTs

accepted.s: NPCIL has equity participation in BHAVINI in connection with the:
accepted.x: NPCIL holds equity in BHAVINI, which is associated with the fast breeder reactor programme.
accepted.tq: Match the organisation with its specialised reactor programme.

accepted.s: The International Atomic Energy Agency (IAEA) was established in:
accepted.x: The IAEA was established in 1957.
accepted.tq: Distinguish the agency’s founding year from the NPT year.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the IAEA?
o: A private organisation headquartered in Geneva with fewer than 50 members
A treaty that entered into force in 1970
An autonomous body in the United Nations system with approximately 180 members
A military alliance responsible for nuclear deterrence
accepted.x: The IAEA is an autonomous body in the UN system and has approximately 180 members.
accepted.tq: Identify the institutional character and membership rather than its headquarters alone.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: India’s membership status in the IAEA is correctly stated as:
o: India joined as a founding member in 1957.
India is not a member of the IAEA.
India joined only after signing the NPT in 1970.
India became a member after the 2008 India–US civil nuclear agreement.
accepted.x: India is a founding member of the IAEA and joined it in 1957.
accepted.tq: Use the membership date to reject treaty-based and post-2008 distractors.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: Which of the following is NOT a function associated with the IAEA?
o: Commanding the military forces of member states
accepted.x: The IAEA undertakes safeguards, verification, safety standards, nuclear security and technical cooperation, but it does not command member states’ military forces.
accepted.tq: Find the option outside the agency’s technical and verification mandate.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: When the IAEA detects non-compliance with safeguards obligations, it may report the matter to the:
accepted.x: The IAEA can report safeguards non-compliance to the United Nations Security Council.
accepted.tq: Identify the correct international authority linked to safeguards violations.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: The IAEA’s ITDB is associated with:
accepted.x: The Incident and Trafficking Database (ITDB) is associated with nuclear security information.
accepted.tq: Decode the specialised database by its institutional context.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding India-specific safeguards:
1. India placed civilian nuclear facilities under IAEA safeguards after the India–US civil nuclear understanding.
2. Military nuclear facilities are covered by the same safeguards arrangement.
3. Imported uranium is intended only for safeguarded reactors.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
accepted.x: Civilian facilities were placed under safeguards to enable fuel imports, while military facilities are excluded. Imported uranium goes only to safeguarded reactors.
accepted.tq: Spot the scope reversal between civilian and military facilities.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: The main purpose of India’s 2006 separation plan in the civil nuclear context was to:
o: place all military facilities under IAEA inspection
separate civilian and military facilities and place the civilian facilities under safeguards
withdraw India from all international nuclear cooperation
accepted.x: The separation plan identified civilian facilities for IAEA safeguards, thereby enabling NSG members to supply nuclear fuel while excluding military facilities.
accepted.tq: Apply the policy objective to a civil-versus-military scenario.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: India signed the IAEA Additional Protocol in 2009, and it entered into force in:
accepted.x: India signed the Additional Protocol in 2009, and it entered into force in 2014.
accepted.tq: Keep the signing year distinct from the entry-into-force year.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: The Additional Protocol applicable to India provides the IAEA with:
o: authority to operate India’s nuclear power plants
wider access for inspection of India’s declared civilian facilities
unrestricted access to all Indian military installations
the power to approve India’s defence budget
accepted.x: The Additional Protocol gives the IAEA wider inspection access, limited to India’s declared civilian facilities.
accepted.tq: Apply the qualification ‘declared civilian facilities’ to avoid an overbroad statement.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: Which statement regarding the Nuclear Non-Proliferation Treaty (NPT) is correct?
o: It was created through the 2008 India–US civil nuclear agreement.
It was signed in 1957 and entered into force in 1968.
It was signed in 1970 and India joined it in 2005.
It was signed in 1968, entered into force in 1970, and India has never signed it.
accepted.x: The NPT dates from 1968, entered into force in 1970, and India has never signed it.
accepted.tq: Separate the treaty dates from the dates of IAEA agreements.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: India’s non-signature of the NPT contributed to its pursuit of:
o: exclusive dependence on imported enriched uranium
accepted.x: Since India did not sign the NPT and its post-1970 weapons capability was treated as outside the treaty framework, it pursued full fuel-cycle independence.
accepted.tq: Link the treaty position with its policy consequence.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s:
Arrange the Nuclear Security Summits in chronological order:
A. Seoul
B. Washington, first summit
C. Washington, fourth summit
D. The Hague
accepted.x: The summits were held at Washington in 2010, Seoul in 2012, The Hague in 2014 and Washington in 2016.
accepted.tq: Fix the first and last summits, then place the two intermediate venues by year.
accepted.sec: IAEA and non-proliferation

accepted.s: ICONS is the abbreviation associated with the IAEA’s:
accepted.x: ICONS refers to the IAEA’s International Conference on Nuclear Security.
